headline: President Bush assigned certain duties under a 2003 global HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria law to specific federal officials.
what_it_does: This order hands out responsibilities created by the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003 to particular officials in the executive branch. That law set up US efforts to fight these diseases in other countries. No summary was provided, so the exact duties and which officials received them are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and officials running global health programs
who_it_affects.how: They are given specific duties for carrying out the 2003 HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria law.

when_it_takes_effect: 2004-11-16 (date signed; exact effective date not stated in the source)
